title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Ava Thompson
body:
Overview

This document is a single, consolidated reference for new and existing Redwood employees covering: working culture and expectations, role families and career ladders, benefits & perks, the hiring and onboarding process, and how to get access to and use our core internal tools. It is intended for broad consumption across the company and maintained by People Ops.

Table of contents
1. Working at Redwood — principles and expectations
2. Roles and career ladders (high level)
3. Benefits & perks (summary and policy links)
4. Hiring & onboarding overview (process and checklists)
5. Internal tools guide (access and common tasks)
6. Ownership, FAQs and references

1) Working at Redwood — principles and expectations

Short intro
Redwood is a developer-first, mission-driven company. We prioritize reliable, high-performance inference and a culture that supports engineering rigor, customer focus, and sustainable growth. The following principles guide day-to-day work:

- Ship quality: prefer small, well-tested changes with clear rollouts and observability.
- Operate with ownership: teams are responsible for design, rollout, and on-call coverage for services they own.
- Communicate early and often: asynchronous updates in team channels + weekly demos keeps cross-functional alignment.
- Continuous learning: invest time in learning, postmortems, and knowledge sharing.
- Diversity of thought and psychological safety: feedback is expected, and discussions focus on improvement not blame.

Working modes and expectations
- Remote-first with optional hubs: teams can choose hybrid rhythms; your manager will document team-level expectations (core hours, optional weekly in-person syncs, etc.).
- Meeting etiquette: add agendas, clearly labeled goals, and time-boxed sessions. Default to async for status unless a decision requires synchronous discussion.
- Time off: use flexible PTO. Coordinate with your manager for coverage on long absences.

2) Roles and career ladders (high level)

We maintain role families and ladders to make expectations and growth paths explicit. This section summarizes families and where to find the detailed ladders.

Role families (examples)
- Engineering: SWE I / II / III / Senior / Staff / Principal
- Applied ML & Research: ML Engineer I / II / Senior / Staff
- Product: PM I / II / Senior / Group PM
- Design: Product Designer I / II / Senior
- SRE/Infra: SRE I / II / Senior / Staff
- Customer Success / Support: CSM / Senior CSM / Solutions Eng

Career ladder highlights (what managers and ICs should expect)
- Competency areas: technical depth, ownership & impact, cross-team collaboration, mentorship, and product sense (where applicable).
- Promotion cadence: typical minimum time-in-role is 12 months, but promotions are based on demonstrated impact and readiness, not just tenure.
- Evidence for promotion: project summaries, manager & peer feedback, metrics (SLOs improved, customer outcomes), and a promotion packet submitted to People Ops.

Career development practices
- 1:1s: required weekly or biweekly depending on role — use them for growth conversations.
- Quarterly calibration: managers meet with People Ops and department leads for leveling alignment.
- Mentorship & learning budget: every employee gets a learning stipend (see benefits).

Where to find full ladders and rubrics
- Full, role-specific ladders and competency rubrics are maintained in the People Ops Confluence space and linked from team charters. For an official ladder, see: /confluence/company-handbook/company-handbook-employee-resources-2026.json

3) Benefits & perks (summary and links)

Redwood provides a competitive benefits package designed to support health, financial security, and work-life balance. Below is a summary; procedural details and eligible plans are available in Benefits Portal (link in People Ops page).

Health & wellness
- Medical, dental, and vision plans with employer subsidy; multiple plan tiers to choose from.
- Mental health support: EAP + covered therapy sessions.
- Wellness stipend: $200/year.

Pay & financial benefits
- Competitive base salary + equity grant at hire; regular market reviews.
- 401(k) plan with employer match (US employees) — match up to 4% after eligibility period.
- Parental leave: 18 weeks primary caregiver, 12 weeks secondary caregiver (paid, job-protected).

Time off & flexible work
- Flexible PTO (guidelines in People Ops policy).
- Company holidays + 1 floating day for personal observance.
- Volunteer time off: 4 hours/year to use for approved volunteer activities.

Learning & growth perks
- Learning stipend: $1,200/year for books, conferences, and courses.
- Conference policy: submit requests to manager and People Ops at least 30 days in advance.

Work setup & equipment
- Home office stipend at hire ($750) and refresh every 36 months.
- Standard dev kit provisioned: laptop (MacBook or approved Linux laptop), monitor budget, and accessories.

Other perks
- Commuter benefits (where applicable), paid volunteer days, monthly team budgets for offsites, company retreats, and regular all-hands.

How to access benefits & who to contact
- Benefits Portal: People Ops intranet page (link).
- Contact: benefits@redwood.com for plan questions, payroll@redwood.com for pay or tax questions, people-ops@redwood.com for policy clarifications.

4) Hiring & onboarding overview (process and checklists)

Hiring process summary (high level)
1. Role creation: hiring manager fills a requisition template and secures headcount approval with Finance and People Ops.
2. Sourcing & screening: Recruiter posts role, screens candidates, and runs an initial phone screen.
3. Interview loop: standardized loop lists technical/role-specific exercises, paired sessions, and a final cross-functional interview.
4. Hiring committee: a small panel reviews feedback, calibrates scoring, and approves the hire.
5. Offer: Compensation team prepares an offer; recruiter extends offer and coordinates background check and references.
6. Acceptance & paperwork: candidate signs offer, People Ops completes onboarding paperwork and sets start date.

Standard interview loop (example for engineering)
- Recruiter screen (30m): high-level fit and role context.
- Technical take-home (optional): 2-4 hour exercise with a clear rubric.
- Onsite loop (virtual): coding + system design + product/contextual + culture/values interview.
- Hiring manager debrief: collects consolidated feedback and scores.

Offer approvals and salary bands
- All offers must be approved by Hiring Manager, Department Head, and Compensation/People Ops.
- Salary bands/ranges are published internally and updated annually during budget planning.

New hire onboarding checklist (People Ops + Manager responsibilities)
- Before start date (People Ops): create account skeletons, send welcome packet, set up payroll and benefits enrollment, and order equipment.
- Before start date (Manager): schedule first week calendar, assign buddy, prepare 30/60/90 day plan, and provide onboarding reading list.
- Day 1 (People Ops): orientation session, benefits overview, IT policies, and security training.
- First week (Manager): team intros, systems access review, and the first onboarding project.
- First 30/60/90 days (Manager & Mentor): weekly 1:1, feedback checkpoints, and a small, measurable onboarding deliverable.

30/60/90-day onboarding template (short)
- 0-30 days: Focus on learning systems, codebase orientation, shadowing, and shipping a small bugfix or doc improvement.
- 31-60 days: Own a small feature/component, participate in on-call rotation (if applicable), and present a short demo of learning.
- 61-90 days: Deliver a substantive piece of work, get feedback for promotion readiness mapping, and propose a growth plan.

Hiring & interview hygiene (mandatory)
- Interviewers must use the rubric, submit written feedback within 48 hours, and avoid asking illegal or unrelated personal questions.
- Recruiters and hiring managers must follow inclusive hiring practices.

5) Internal tools guide (access and common tasks)

Core tools and purpose
- Slack: company communication. Use public channels for cross-team signals and private channels for sensitive discussions.
- GitHub: code hosting and PR workflow. Repos are organized by product area; use labels and PR templates.
- Linear: issue tracking and sprint planning (team boards).
- Confluence: documentation and runbooks (this content lives here).
- Okta: SSO provider for enterprise apps.
- 1Password: company credentials vault.
- GSuite (Gmail, Drive, Calendar): email, document collaboration, and calendaring.
- Datadog / Observability dashboards: production monitoring and alerting (access via SSO).

Access requests and typical flows
- New hire provisioning (automatic for most roles): People Ops triggers provisioning through IT; expect access to Slack, email, and primary tools on Day 1.
- Additional access (datastores, production consoles, billing): requires manager approval + owner_service ticket.
- Emergency access: use the on-call escalation process documented in the eng-sre space; ephemeral elevated access is granted via just-in-time approvals and audited.

Common tasks and quick how-tos
- Request a GitHub repo: open an issue in the infra-team repo with team name, repo purpose, and initial collaborators.
- Set up dev environment: follow team README -> clone repository -> run ./dev/start (team-specific).
- Request Datadog dashboard access: submit a ticket to observability@redwood.com with the dashboard name and justification.
- Submit an infra change: open a PR against terraform repos and follow the CI/CD pipeline; include rollout & rollback steps in PR description.

Security and credential hygiene
- MFA is required on all accounts.
- Store secrets in the approved vault (1Password and our secrets service); do not store credentials in Git.
- Production access requires approval and is rotated regularly.

6) Ownership, FAQs and references

Document ownership
- Maintained by: People Ops (primary) with contributions from Engineering Manager leads for role ladders and Finance for compensation policies.
- Update cadence: quarterly reviews or as policy changes.

Common FAQs
- Q: How do I request parental leave?
  A: Email benefits@redwood.com and submit leave requests via the People Ops portal.
- Q: Who approves conference attendance?
  A: Your manager approves; People Ops must sign off for budget over $1500.
- Q: How do I raise a concern about leveling?
  A: Discuss with your manager; if unresolved, escalate to People Ops for a calibration review.

References and links
- People Ops home: /confluence/company-handbook/company-handbook-employee-resources-2026.json
- Full role ladders: People Ops ladders page (linked from People Ops home).
- Benefits & payroll: Benefits Portal link on People Ops home.
